correctness.rationale: Lemma 5.2 of arXiv:2610.05384v1 proves that a crossing-free path has at most \(2L_{2n-2}\) edges. A height-\(2n\) subtree attains this by traversing both root children while replacing every bottom cutoff vertex by its \(a\)-jump; the path has \(2L_{2n-2}\) edges and visits only one interior grid height. Hence the exact threshold is \(2L_{2n-2}+1=6\cdot4^{n-1}-3\). Section 6 then runs unchanged with this threshold. Finite dynamic-programming checks reproduce equality for \(1\le n\le6\) at height \(2n\) and for \(1\le n\le4\) at height \(3n\).

value.rationale: The first-crossing threshold controls the central nilpotency step of the new simple-nil-ring construction. Determining its exact value is a natural structural boundary, and it lowers the uniform exponent used in that step from \(2\cdot4^n\) to \(\tfrac32\cdot4^n-3\), an asymptotic factor \(3/4\). The result pinpoints exactly where slack remains and where it does not, without claiming an improvement to the separate compression bound.
